solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Troubled co-star shunning second player?

indicators.note: troubled letters are disturbed and thrown into a new order
shunning means keeping away from, so this letter is left out of the fodder

explanation.surface: A film star with a difficult co-star avoids a second performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shunning' drops S from CO-STAR, leaving COTAR, which 'Troubled' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage performer is a player in the theatrical sense; the question mark flags the less obvious sporting reading.

clue.text: One criticising later, losing head about cheap stuff

indicators.note: about means the shortened word goes around the other piece
losing head means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
tack is tacky, cheap and showy merchandise

explanation.surface: Someone who criticises tawdry goods after the event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' leaves ATER, which goes 'about' the cheap stuff; tack is cheap, gaudy goods, the root of tacky.
explanation.definitionFit: A critic who lays into something is said to attack it, so a fierce critic is an assailant.

clue.text: Flummox heartless tough — dispute follows

indicators.note: follows places the dispute word after the first piece
heartless means the inner letters of the word are removed, leaving only its ends

parts.note: a row is a quarrel or dispute

explanation.surface: A cruel, unfeeling bully baffles someone and then an argument breaks out.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw someone is an informal synonym for disconcerting or confusing them.

clue.text: One painting home first to praise high point resistant to moisture

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist elected to the Royal Academy
in means at home

indicators.note: first to points at the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the roof is the top of a building

explanation.surface: An artist at home sets out to praise a summit that withstands the wet.
explanation.walkthrough: RA, a Royal Academician, is a crossword staple for a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something waterproof against showers keeps out damp, which is exactly being impervious to moisture.

clue.text: Publicise drink additive?

definitions.meaning: to feature prominently in the press, as with a front-page story
a small dash of soda or water added to a drink such as whisky

explanation.surface: Advertising some extra ingredient for a beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper can give a story prominence on page one, and a barman adds a little soda to a whisky.

clue.text: Advice about mine

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tip is a helpful piece of advice

explanation.surface: Guidance concerning a mine.
explanation.definitionFit: A coal mine is commonly called a colliery shaft or simply a pit.

clue.text: Some attendees in atrium brought up spicy item?

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
Some says only part of the following words is taken, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Guests in a hall serve up something spicy.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters DEESINA run across 'attendees in atrium'; 'brought up' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: The seed of the anise plant is a liquorice-flavoured spice used in cooking and drinks.

clue.text: Hearts on top of tree — leadership position

indicators.note: on top of in a down clue places the first piece above the second

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games such as bridge
an elm is a deciduous tree

explanation.surface: Hearts set on the crown of a tree mark the top job.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at the helm, the steering wheel of a ship, idiomatically means being in charge.

clue.text: Principal feature of abnormally nice peer, etc

indicators.note: abnormally means the letters are arranged in an unusual way

explanation.surface: The main point about an oddly pleasant nobleman and the like.
explanation.definitionFit: The focal item of a display or table is its showpiece, the principal feature.

clue.text: Enemy of wood in school time, biter at heart?

parts.note: a term is a division of the school year

indicators.note: at heart means the central letters of the word are taken

explanation.surface: A wood-eating pest turns up during term, a biter by nature.
explanation.definitionFit: These insects, sometimes called white ants, eat timber and so destroy wooden structures.

clue.text: Time and volition to get fabric

parts.note: will is the power of choosing, volition

explanation.surface: Someone finds the time and determination to obtain some cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A woven cloth with diagonal ribs, used for jeans and trousers, is a type of textile.

clue.text: Intimidate farm animal

definitions.meaning: to subdue someone by bullying or frightening them
a female bovine kept for milk

explanation.surface: Bullying livestock on a farm.
explanation.definitionFit: To overawe someone is a verb sense, and a dairy beast is the noun sense of the same word.

clue.text: One acting desultorily, Harry meeting Queen?

parts.note: Harry Potter is the boy wizard of the J K Rowling novels
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A schoolboy wizard meets the monarch and is a bit aimless.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the late Queen Elizabeth's royal cipher.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who putters around does small tasks in an aimless, unhurried way.

clue.text: Running away to join up? Open, let me out!

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are released and rearranged

explanation.surface: A cry from someone locked in, desperate to run off and get married.
explanation.definitionFit: Eloping is a couple fleeing secretly to marry, so 'join up' plays on joining in wedlock.

clue.text: Chart — it's associated with English form of carbon

parts.note: a graph is a chart of data
the word it, with the 's (is) acting as a link

explanation.surface: A diagram showing that it is linked to England.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft black material in pencils is crystalline carbon, one of that element's allotropes.

clue.text: Creed (Lord's one) converted this group?

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form, so the letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A religious creed, the Lord's own, has turned a community to faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloistered religious community, such as monks or nuns cut off from the world, is a group living by a creed.

clue.text: Instrument in car I've adapted safeguarding learner

indicators.note: safeguarding means protecting, so the rearranged letters surround the other piece
adapted means modified, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is for learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A musical keyboard fits in a converted car that protects a learner driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' rearranges CARIVE, which goes round L by 'safeguarding'.
explanation.definitionFit: A clavier is a keyboard instrument such as a harpsichord or clavichord.

clue.text: Newspaper I am getting in healthy period of rest

indicators.note: in means these pieces are placed inside the other word

parts.note: hale means robustly healthy
FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper
I'm is the contraction of I am

explanation.surface: Reading the paper keeps me fit and gives me a break.
explanation.walkthrough: FT and IM go 'in' HALE: HAL-FTIM-E.
explanation.definitionFit: The interval in a match when players take a break is the rest period between halves.

clue.text: Not quite mature, move rapidly

indicators.note: Not quite means the word stops short, losing its final letter

parts.note: ripe means fully mature, like fruit

explanation.surface: Something not yet fully grown takes off at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear along is to go very fast, as in 'let it rip'.

clue.text: Lacking consistency — amusing with beginning changed

indicators.note: with beginning changed means the opening letter is swapped for another

parts.note: funny means amusing

explanation.surface: A comic routine that falls flat when its opening is altered.
explanation.walkthrough: The replacement letter R comes from the answer itself: F becomes R.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquid that is too thin and flows easily, like a soft egg yolk, lacks thickness.

clue.text: Discontinue street work

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Halt the roadworks on a street.
explanation.definitionFit: To cease or halt something is to bring it to an end, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Group that remains identified by ethnicity first of all

indicators.note: first of all means the opening letter of every one of these words is taken

explanation.surface: A community whose remains are identified by ethnic origin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribe is a social division of people sharing descent and culture, a kind of group.

clue.text: Consume beef, say, when starter's off?

indicators.note: starter's off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: beef is an example of meat, flagged by 'say'

explanation.surface: A diner wonders whether to eat the beef once the first course has been cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' looks like the first course of a meal but means the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To consume food is simply to take it in as a meal.

clue.text: Portion of cosmetic henna in Madras once

indicators.note: Portion of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some henna, used as a cosmetic, comes from an Indian city.
explanation.definitionFit: The south Indian city formerly called Madras was officially renamed in 1996.

clue.text: Private investigator to think highly of law-breaker?

parts.note: to rate someone is to regard them highly

explanation.surface: A detective admires a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: A buccaneer or copyright infringer is an outlaw, and the question mark covers both senses.

clue.text: Your old extremely mature shrub

parts.note: thy is the archaic form of your

indicators.note: extremely means the extreme letters, first and last, of the word are taken

explanation.surface: Your very old, fully grown bush.
explanation.definitionFit: This aromatic herb grows as a small woody plant, technically a low bush.
